main_text.p: λήθ ἔ χέιν (pro χέω dicitur etiam χείω) quòd multas fundat pluvias & nives, sicut & ipsa Latina vox origine Græca ὗω τὶ νεὶν a pluendo.

Χειμάρρῳ·ς ὁ torrens, ex χειμα΄ ὢ· τὸ hyems, tempestas, & ῥόῳ· ς ὁ fluxus, q.d. ῥόῳ· Ἐ χει- μάτος. ῥόῳ· ῆς, ὁς ς, ὁ fluxus a ῥέω, in futu- ro ῥύσω. prat. ἐῤῥύηκα. prat. med. ἐῤῥόα, unde est ῥόῳ· fluxus. Confer ὡσ̈ρρέω.

Χεὶρ χάρος ἡ manus, Actor.28.3. gratia & bene- dictio Dei, Luc.1. v.66. potestas, Luc.1.74. Johan.3.35. potentia, Actor.11. v.21. vindi- cta, Act.13.v.11. pravus affectus, quem per manum exferimus, Matth.5.v.39. machina- tio, Luc.22.21. Confer 2.Reg.14.19. ἐν χεῖρ̈ ב״ יד idem quod per. Actor.7.35. ἀξ χειρῶν idem Actor.19.10. Notetur phrasis, ἐπιθέ- νεῖ τινὶ χειρα, imponere alicui manum, quo gestu Apostoli usi fuisse leguntur in creandis verbi ministris, 1.Tim.5.22. a personis or- dinandis, ut loquuntur, Num.27.18. item a bestiis sacrificandis, quibus manus olim (Exod.29. v.10.) imponebatur, gestu huc translato, quo indicare voluerunt, perso- nam hanc DEO inprimis confecratam.
Χειραγωγὸς ὁ ἡ qui vel quæ manu ducit. ex χείρ χάρος ἡ manus, & ἀγωγὸς ὁ ἡ dux via, Th.ἄγω, Act.13.11.
Χειραγωγέω ῶ manu duco. Fut. ἡσω. Prat. κεχει- ραγώγηκα.

page.notes: The Greek and Hebrew in this page are only approximately legible at the scan resolution; accents and breathings are uncertain and several Greek words are marked as readings from the scan rather than certain letters. The left-hand strip (margin of the previous page, with Greek and Latin notes) is largely cut off and illegible and is omitted.
